newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Benefits seen for BCP in BPA capital call.
newsitem.headline: Benefits seen for BCP in BPA capital call.

text.p: Shareholders in Banco Comercial Portugues will gain medium-term from the 85 billion escudo capital call announced for subsidiary Banco Portugues do Atlantico because it will strengthen the latter's commercial operations, analysts said.
"I believe the share price of BCP will not be penalised...not least because it (the call) was already expected," said Cristina Fonseca of ESR-Espirito Santo Research.
"Over the medium term, the bigger share capital of BPA, the greater its capacity to make loans, which is positive for BCP," said Miguel Viana of brokers Tottadealer.
BCP announced on Wednesday that BPA, of which it has just over 50 percent, would be boosting capital through the issue of preference shares and perpetual bonds.

According to one source close to the operation, if BCP follows the same course as in other group operations, it is likely to issue up to 45 billion escudos of non-voting preference shares through a foreign subsidiary.
BCP should subscribe to virtually the full amount of the offer, the source said.

Following the operation, BPA's capital adequacy ratio should rise to around 10.5 percent from the current eight percent, while the consolidated adequacy ratio of BCP will rise to around 10 percent from 9.3 percent.
The remainder of BPA's capital is in the hands of insurer Imperio.
"This confirms the intention of the group to use an increase in the activity of BPA as a source of growth. This will bring dividends to BCP as well," said an analyst at an investment bank.
Analysts said that it was a logical move looking towards the long-term future of the group with Imperio having an option to sell which BCP must decide whether to take up or not.
"It is logical to boost BPA's capital either to buy the remaining 50 percent with a lower goodwill or to make it easier to place the remaining 50 percent with a partner," said one analyst.
"The operation is logical because from March 1997 (BCP) could have to consolidate fully BPA or find a buyer for Imperio's stake," echoed Miguel Viana.
